prior_hypotheses:
- Thalamic Spindle Modulation via Thalamocortical Coupling and White Matter Integrity in Sleep Phenotypes: This hypothesis integrates thalamocortical coupling and white matter integrity to explain spindle modulation and sleep phenotypes, leveraging mechanisms from both P1 and P2.
- Thalamic Spindle Refractory Period Modulation via Thalamocortical Coupling: Epileptic thalamic spikes increase the thalamic spindle refractory period, modulating thalamocortical coupling and spindle density during sleep.
- White Matter Integrity Modulates Thalamocortical Spindle Overlap via Fractional Anisotropy: This hypothesis proposes that fractional anisotropy (FA) in white matter tracts modulates the topographical patterns of thalamocortical spindle overlap, influencing the differentiation between slow and fast spindle subtypes during sleep.
- Thalamic Spindle Modulation via Thalamocortical Coupling in Sleep Phenotypes: This hypothesis explores how thalamic spindle modulation through thalamocortical coupling influences sleep phenotypes, integrating evidence from spindle activity and thalamocortical functional connectivity.
